courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

lectures.title: Starting Work on a New Offer Form

cues.en: Let's work on that new offer page and for that, I'm in the places offer new offer folder and here's the
new-offer.html
file. Here I had my grid playground, I don't need that anymore so let's remove that, I will
work with the ion-grid though
but now in a more beautiful way and indeed, I will use the grid and not ion-list here to structure my
different inputs because I always want to have some input sit next to each other now and that will not
work with the ion-list, that only positions items from top to bottom.
So let's start
and first of all, I'll assign a size here for this column and I'll make sure that if we are on smaller
devices or bigger, we only take six columns and I add my offset-sm of three here and then I'll start
with the first ion-item that will wrap my first ion-label and ion-input here and the first input
is all about the title of the place we're offering.
So I'll give this a label of title and then add ion-input type text here.
Now what I haven't shown you thus far but what you can set on these inputs here are other special
attributes Ionic supports, like autocomplete and autocorrect
and they will do just what it sounds like,
they will make sure that especially also on real mobile devices, you get autocorrection and autocompletion
turned on and of course you can omit this if you don't want that behavior or explicitly set it to false
even
but here I will add it, also to show these attributes you can set and that is then my title here.
Now we're not done with a title,
I also want to allow users to enter a description and therefore in a new ion-row, I'll add another
ion-column which will get the same sizing and offset as the first column and in this ion-column, I'll
add yet another ion-item with an
ion-label in it which is our short description for the place we're creating
and there, I'll add an ion-text-area actually. Just as we have a text area
in normal HTML, Ionic also has one and just as in normal HTML, the ion-text-area simply is an input that
can span across multiple lines and allows us to enter longer text.
Now by the way since I forgot it, both labels should have a position of floating,
so let me add it to the title label and then of course also to the short description label here.
Now back to the text area,
just as on the text area HTML element, you can add a rows attribute and set this to the amount
of rows this text area should show as a default
and I'll set this to three
and in general, you can configure this as you can configure the normal HTML text area and check
the official Ionic docs to learn all about these components and how you can configure them, which attributes
they support and so on.
So that's the text area. Below that, I want to have an input for the price and therefore I'll just copy that
first ion-row with the title in there, edit here and replace the title label here with price and this
will be of type number because users should indeed enter a number here and not some text and therefore, I
don't need autocompletion or autocorrection on there. So thus far, the text area is new but other than
that, it's pretty standard.
Now let's have a look at a component that is not that much of a standard component but that is pretty
common in mobile apps and that is pretty powerful.
